details.text:
The buyer is the VP of Engineering or Head of Platform at a Series A to C software-led startup with 30 to 150 developers using modern, fast-moving stacks, whose team culture skews toward high-velocity power users (heavy Vim, Raycast, and GitHub CLI adopters). They are actively losing engineering velocity and morale to context-switching inside bloated, mouse-driven tools like Jira, resulting in sluggish sprint updates and team friction. This individual holds discretionary engineering tooling budget up to $10,000–$20,000 annually without extensive enterprise procurement friction, and prioritizes developer experience (DevEx) and retention above rigid compliance reporting.

Globally, there are approximately 26 million software developers, representing a Total Addressable Market (TAM) of roughly $3.1 billion annually assuming full developer adoption at a standard $10/seat/month. Narrowing down to the Serviceable Addressable Market (SAM) of roughly 1.2 million engineers at venture-backed, high-velocity tech startups and modern mid-market product companies yields a $144 million annual market. Assuming a conservative 3% to 5% Serviceable Obtainable Market (SOM) penetration within this segment through bottom-up developer adoption converting into company-wide licenses at $12/seat/month, the near-term addressable market opportunity stands at 36,000 to 60,000 paid seats, representing $5.2 million to $8.6 million in Annual Recurring Revenue (ARR).
